title: 🤖 Dots Agents Reach ChatGPT Plus Subscribers — Working for You While You Sleep!
body: 🤖 Dots Agents Reach ChatGPT Plus Subscribers — Working for You While You Sleep!

OpenAI has begun testing its persistent agents, Dots, with a small group of subscribers on the ChatGPT Plus plan, which costs $20 a month, after the feature was previously exclusive to the pricier plans.

Dots are AI agents that work continuously without supervision: each has its own cloud computer, keeps working on your task between conversations, can access more than 4,000 apps, and can even control your computer on your behalf — and you can follow its progress at any time.

The service had been available since launch to Pro subscribers at $100 a month and large business plans, but now it also reaches all ChatGPT Business Standard users in the United States, with every eligible user getting one personal agent at no extra cost.

The agents now run on the GPT-6.1 Terra and GPT-6 Astra models, and the company added new features including an iPhone widget, integration with Shortcuts, and support for text messages and replying to notifications directly from the phone.

But the test is limited: a Plus subscriber cannot request access — the agent either appears in their account or it doesn't — and the company has not said whether it will stay permanently or end after the test; the feature is also unavailable in Europe, the UK, Switzerland, and Korea.

Simply put: imagine an employee working for you all night — researching, preparing, and organizing — so you wake up to find the task done; that is what Dots does, and now it is closer to ordinary subscribers.
Would you trust an AI agent working alone on your computer while you sleep?
